note: Moderate-to-severe Crohn's: anti-mouse IL-23p19 surrogate antibodies treated T-cell-transfer and anti-CD40 colitis (2007 on) and the IL23R R381Q loss-of-function allele protects people from Crohn's (2006); risankizumab (2017 phase 2, 2022 phase 3, approved June 2022), brazikumab (2017 phase 2a; development stopped 2023) and mirikizumab (2021 phase 2, 2024 phase 3) all beat placebo, while cynomolgus toxicology at 1.3x the 600 mg IV exposure was silent on the hepatotoxicity that emerged in Crohn's induction; no model picks which patients respond.
label: Crohn's (anti-IL-23)

engagement.model: T-cell transfer colitis mouse (anti-mouse IL-23p19 mAb)
engagement.note: Anti-IL-23p19 down-regulated colonic inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in transferred-T-cell colitis; no patient readout yet.
engagement.short: Anti-p19 lowered colonic cytokines in mice
engagement.quote: Monoclonal anti-IL-23p19 prevented and treated active colitis, with down-regulation of a broad array of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in the colon.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level reading (PMID 17570211). The antibody was an anti-mouse p19 mAb, not a class member (product_in_model false). Model first use 2007 for an anti-p19 antibody; p19-knockout work (Yen 2006, doi:10.1172/JCI21404) is genetic, not antibody, and is not opened as a track.

engagement.magnitude_basis: IL-23/IL-17-axis cytokine and transcript levels in gut tissue
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC6225973); paired by me, mouse cytokine protein/mRNA versus human RNA-seq.
engagement.model: T-cell transfer colitis mouse (anti-mouse IL-23p19 mAb)
engagement.note: Risankizumab lowered IL-23/IL-17-axis transcripts in colon and ileum biopsies of Crohn's patients at week 12, as anti-p19 did in mouse colon.
engagement.short: IL-23/IL-17 transcripts fell in patient biopsies
engagement.quote: Differentiated expression of genes associated with the IL-23/IL-17 axis was observed in the colon and ileum 12 weeks after risankizumab treatment.
engagement.reason: Colonic IL-23/IL-17 readout fell in patients
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): Visvanathan does not cite the mouse data. Readout is downstream (axis transcripts, not IL-23 occupancy). Direction only; the quantities are not commensurable. Feagan 2017 CRP/calprotectin falls would give the same call a year earlier but are not the mouse readout.

dose.model: T-cell transfer colitis mouse (anti-mouse IL-23p19 mAb)
dose.note: Surrogate anti-mouse p19 antibodies set no human exposure target; Crohn's dosing came from psoriasis PK and the human phase 2.
dose.short: Mouse surrogate sets no exposure target
dose.quote: Monoclonal anti-IL-23p19 was administered at the same time as or 4 weeks after pathogenic CD4 T-cell transfer.
dose.judgement: Not an empty cell: a model existed and was used, but a surrogate antibody dosed at 15 mg/kg IP (FDA BLA 761262 review) cannot translate to a human regimen. The FDA review says the phase 2 study, not any model, 'supported the dose selection for induction treatment in phase 3'.

dose.note: Monkeys tolerated 50 mg/kg/week risankizumab for 6 months; psoriasis review, no Crohn's exposure to compare yet.
dose.quote: There were no treatment-related effects on respiratory rate or body temperature in Cynomolgus monkeys subcutaneously treated with doses up to 50 mg/kg/week risankizumab for 6 months.
dose.judgement: Opener for the toxicology track at its first public date (psoriasis BLA review, April 2019); the monkey studies predate it but were unpublished.

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL AUC over human 600 mg IV induction AUC
dose.confidence_note: The margin is thin (1.3x) and hepatotoxicity emerged at the 600 mg IV dose; scored same under decision 16 because the dose was reached and approved, with the unpredicted harm counted once in safety.
dose.note: The monkey NOAEL (50 mg/kg/week) sat 1.3x above the 600 mg IV Crohn's induction exposure, and patients were dosed to that target.
dose.short: NOAEL 1.3x above 600 mg IV exposure held
dose.quote: The 50 mg/kg dose in monkeys provides approximately 1.3 times the exposure (AUC) in humans administered the 600 mg induction regimen, and 3.1 times the exposure in humans administered the 360 mg maintenance regimen for CD.
dose.reason: Dosed to target within the monkey margin
dose.judgement: Decision 16: a stated tolerability margin that held. The reviewer approved 600 mg IV as 'the lowest effective dosage'; no toxicity block. A stricter reader could call the 1.3x margin misplaced and score contra with blocked_by toxicity, but the dose was never lowered, so I did not.

dose.model: Sponsor population-PK / exposure-response dose model from phase 2 (risankizumab; mirikizumab pooled)
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6373392). The paper reports PK only and says the Crohn's exposure-response reports are 'planned'; the phase 2 exposure-response read that chose 600 mg IV for phase 3 (started May 2017) is public only through the FDA review.
dose.note: Phase I/II popPK model (incl. Crohn's phase 2) underpinned the exposure-response read that picked 600 mg IV for phase 3; no phase 3 result yet.
dose.quote: A two-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination described the pharmacokinetics of risankizumab.
dose.judgement: Opens the in-silico track at its first public date (PubMed 2018-08-21; print March 2019). One track for the sponsors' phase 2 popPK/exposure-response dose models (AbbVie risankizumab; Lilly mirikizumab, CTS 2025) under the identity rule: same system class, same prediction (the phase 2 exposure plateau fixes the induction dose). Surrogate mouse dosing (15 mg/kg IP) set no human target, so this is the only model that stated one.

dose.model: Sponsor population-PK / exposure-response dose model from phase 2 (risankizumab; mirikizumab pooled)
dose.magnitude_basis: phase 2 exposure-response-selected induction dose (600 mg IV, predicted Cavg 60.5 mg/L) versus the approved induction dose (600 mg IV); 1200 mg added nothing
dose.confidence_note: Quote from the bundled 761262 IntegratedR text (section 14.4.2). The exposure-response report the review cites (R&D/20/1614) is dated 2020 and pools phase 2 and 3; whether a formal model, rather than the phase 2 dose-response itself, chose 600 mg in 2017 is not stated. Decision 16 does not apply: no tolerability margin was stated by this model.
dose.note: Phase 3 reached the ER-selected 600 mg IV exposures and both coprimaries were met; 1200 mg added nothing, so the model's target was enough.
dose.short: ER-selected 600 mg IV held in phase 3
dose.quote: Model predictions together with observed data indicated that the efficacy may have reached a plateau at 600 mg IV induction regimen with no substantial added benefit from the 1200 mg IV induction regimen.
dose.reason: 600 mg IV reached; phase 3 confirmed plateau
dose.judgement: Dose table case 'reached, drug worked': the regimen the phase 2 exposure-response read chose (600 mg IV at weeks 0, 4, 8) was given in ADVANCE/MOTIVATE (registry 2022-06-14 and 2022-07-06), met both coprimaries, and the 1200 mg arm showed no added benefit, so the target was enough. Maintenance was not model-chosen (no phase 2 dose-ranging; 180 vs 360 mg SC showed no dose-response). The hepatotoxicity at this exposure is counted once, in safety on the cynomolgus track, because this model stated no margin. Tier-1 corroboration that changes no status: Suleiman 2023 CPT (doi 10.1002/cpt.2831, epub 2023-01-20, abstract-level) says the same from phase 2+3 data, and Lilly's mirikizumab model (doi 10.1111/cts.70320, 2025) found VIVID-1's 900 mg result 'aligned with SERENITY'.

efficacy.note: A hypomorphic IL23R allele protects against Crohn's, prioritising IL-23 blockade; no anti-p19 patient data yet.
efficacy.quote: An uncommon coding variant (rs11209026, c.1142G>A, p.Arg381Gln) confers strong protection against Crohn's disease, and additional noncoding IL23R variants are independently associated.
efficacy.judgement: Human genetic track (model_kind human_genetic), separate from the mouse because it is a different system with its own prediction (receptor loss of function protects, so blocking the ligand should treat). model_filed true: the mirikizumab BLA 761279 review cites this GWAS in its background; the risankizumab Crohn's review does not.

efficacy.model: T-cell transfer colitis mouse (anti-mouse IL-23p19 mAb)
efficacy.note: Anti-IL-23p19 prevented and reversed established T-cell-mediated colitis; AbbVie's surrogate later gave 62% endoscopic inhibition in SCID transfer colitis.
efficacy.quote: Inhibition of IL-23p19 was effective in both prevention and treatment of active colitis.
efficacy.judgement: One track for the sponsors' mouse colitis models (T-cell transfer and anti-CD40, risankizumab surrogate PR-963484 in BLA 761262; two unnamed murine IBD models with mirikizumab surrogate LSN2479016 in BLA 761279): same system class, same prediction.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: protective allele direction versus placebo-adjusted clinical remission
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Feagan 2017 (Lancet, paywalled); paired by me with the GWAS.
efficacy.note: Risankizumab 600 mg IV induced clinical remission in moderate-to-severe Crohn's (37% vs 15%), as the protective allele predicted.
efficacy.short: Anti-p19 induced remission as the allele predicted
efficacy.quote: Ten (24%) of 41 patients who received 200 mg risankizumab had clinical remission (9·0%, -8·3 to 26·2; p=0·31) and 15 (37%) of 41 who received the 600 mg dose (20·9%, 2·6 to 39·2; p=0·0252).
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: no source I read puts the R381Q prediction beside the trial. Brazikumab's phase 2a (Sands 2017, epub 2017-04-05, one week earlier) is the earliest positive datum but its primary-outcome sentence exceeds 40 words, so Feagan 2017 (epub 2017-04-12) carries the quote; both are 2017. Direction only. Phase 3 confirmations (ADVANCE/MOTIVATE 2022, VIVID-1 2024) are listed in patient_trials and change no status.

patient_trials.quote: The primary outcome, clinical response (either a 100-point decrease in CD Activity Index score from baseline or clinical remission, defined as CD Activity Index score <150) at week 8 occurred in 49.2% of patients receiving MEDI2070 (n = 59) compared with 26.7% receiving placebo (n = 60; absolute difference, 22.5%; 95% confidence interval, 5.6%-39.5%; P = .010).
Ten (24%) of 41 patients who received 200 mg risankizumab had clinical remission (9·0%, -8·3 to 26·2; p=0·31) and 15 (37%) of 41 who received the 600 mg dose (20·9%, 2·6 to 39·2; p=0·0252).
Mirikizumab effectively induced endoscopic response after 12 weeks in patients with moderate-to-severe CD and demonstrated durable efficacy to Week 52.
All coprimary endpoints at week 12 were met in both trials with both doses of risankizumab (p values ≤0·0001).
All coprimary endpoints at week 12 were met in both trials with both doses of risankizumab (p values ≤0·0001).

Both coprimary endpoints were met: endoscopic response-composite was reached in 220 (38·0%) of 579 patients on mirikizumab versus 18 (9·0%) of 199 on placebo (99·5% CI 20·6-36·8; p<0·0001); CDAI clinical remission-composite was reached in 263 (45·4%) of 579 patients on mirikizumab versus 39 (19·6%) of 199 patients on placebo (99·5% CI 15·9-35·6; p<0·0001).
The study was early terminated and development of brazikumab stopped.

efficacy.note: Risankizumab 600 mg IV induced clinical remission (37% vs 15%) in Crohn's, as anti-p19 treated mouse colitis.

efficacy.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6580782). The ex-vivo antibody was a commercial anti-IL23p19 (R&D Systems), not a class member.
efficacy.note: Apoptosis-resistant TNFR2+IL23R+ T cells expand in anti-TNF non-responders; ex-vivo anti-IL23p19 induced their apoptosis, naming IL-23 as the target in that group.
efficacy.short: IL-23 named as target in anti-TNF failures
efficacy.quote: These findings identify IL-23 as a suitable molecular target in patients with Crohn's disease refractory to anti-TNF therapy.
efficacy.judgement: Opener at first use (epub 2018-05-30). A patient-level system: patient mucosal organ cultures and LPMCs sorted by anti-TNF response, with anti-IL23p19 and IL-23 added ex vivo. Separate from the mouse and genetic tracks because it is a different system with its own prediction (which patients, not whether the class works). model_filed false: neither bundled FDA review cites it.

efficacy.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo T-cell apoptosis / IL-23-axis readout versus phase 2 remission in anti-TNF-experienced patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. The source is the model paper and itself states the comparison, so model_src carries the patient side (Feagan 2017, with Sands 2017 MEDI2070 in patient_trials); both trials were public (April 2017) before the model paper.
efficacy.note: The paper sets its ex-vivo finding beside the 2017 risankizumab and MEDI2070 phase 2 results in anti-TNF-experienced patients and calls them concordant.
efficacy.short: Reproduces phase 2 success in anti-TNF failures
efficacy.quote: Recently published trials showed that risankizumab and MEDI2070, specific inhibitors for IL-23 p19, were remarkably effective in anti-TNF refractory patients with CD.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the phase 2 trials in largely anti-TNF-experienced patients (Feagan 2017 epub 2017-04-12, 93% anti-TNF-experienced; Sands 2017 epub 2017-04-05) were known when the paper framed its aim around them, so retro, not same. The paper itself notes the trials did not compare anti-TNF-naive with -experienced patients, so the match is at population level, direction only.

efficacy.model: Crohn's patient mucosal organ cultures and lamina propria T cells from anti-TNF non-responders (anti-IL23p19 ex vivo)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo prediction that IL-23 blockade works in anti-TNF-refractory patients versus placebo-adjusted CDAI remission in MOTIVATE (biologic failures)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of D'Haens 2022 (Europe PMC rendering; the abstract CI dashes are written as hyphens there). Paired by me; D'Haens does not cite the ex-vivo work.
efficacy.note: MOTIVATE (biologic failures, risankizumab 600 mg IV) met both coprimaries; it retests the claim the 2018 model drew from the 2017 phase 2 results, so the track stays retro.
efficacy.quote: In MOTIVATE, CDAI clinical remission rate was 42% (22%, 13-31; 80/191) with risankizumab 600 mg and 40% (21%, 12-29; 77/191) with risankizumab 1200 mg versus 20% (37/187) with placebo
efficacy.judgement: The first prospective test after the retrodiction (decision 10): MOTIVATE's result (registry 2022-06-14, Lancet May 2022) postdates the 2018 prediction, and its population is exactly the one the model named. Scored same, patient-level, but weakly: the cellular marker (TNFR2+IL23R+ expansion) was never measured in trial patients, and the model's prediction was itself shaped by the phase 2 data, so this is population-level concordance, direction only. Mirikizumab VIVID-1 (2024) and ADVANCE's biologic-failure stratum would add nothing to the status. Ruling (decision 10, check adjudication): MOTIVATE was registered 2017-04-07, its biologic-failure design fixed before the 2018 model, and it retests the phase 2 result the model was framed on; no fresh prospective prediction, so retro, not same, with strengthens true on the retro track.

The primary outcome, clinical response (either a 100-point decrease in CD Activity Index score from baseline or clinical remission, defined as CD Activity Index score <150) at week 8 occurred in 49.2% of patients receiving MEDI2070 (n = 59) compared with 26.7% receiving placebo (n = 60; absolute difference, 22.5%; 95% confidence interval, 5.6%-39.5%; P = .010).
In MOTIVATE, CDAI clinical remission rate was 42% (22%, 13-31; 80/191) with risankizumab 600 mg and 40% (21%, 12-29; 77/191) with risankizumab 1200 mg versus 20% (37/187) with placebo

safety.note: Six months at 50 mg/kg/week produced no treatment-related toxicity in monkeys; nothing in Crohn's patients to compare yet.
safety.quote: There were no treatment-related effects on respiratory rate or body temperature in Cynomolgus monkeys subcutaneously treated with doses up to 50 mg/kg/week risankizumab for 6 months.
safety.judgement: Opener at the toxicology track's first public date. The monkey ePPND study did predict dose-dependent fetal/infant loss, which no human pregnancy dataset has tested, so it stays uncompared.

safety.confidence_note: Signal rests on one probable DILI case plus transaminase patterns across induction studies; the label carries a Warnings and Precautions entry. Monkeys can show liver injury, so the silence counts.
safety.note: Hepatotoxicity (one probable DILI, Hy's-law pattern) emerged with 600 mg IV induction in Crohn's; monkeys at 1.3x that exposure had no clinical-pathology change.
safety.quote: However, a risk of hepatotoxicity related to risankizumab exposure emerged during the safety review of this marketing application that may be attributed to the higher dosage and route of administration proposed for the CD indication.
safety.judgement: Silence contradicted on a harm the species could have shown (clinical pathology was measured and normal at 1.3x the human AUC). Paired within the review, which never states the comparison, so comparison_stated false with the psoriasis-BLA monkey data as model_src. Counted here, not in dose, because the monkey did not predict it. Class corroboration: the mirikizumab UC review (BLA 761279, 2023) also found 'A risk of hepatotoxicity related to mirikizumab' with clean monkeys; being another indication it would be imported and changes nothing. magnitude null: a missed harm has no model number.
